declaration.preface:
Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. is committed to protecting the environment, promoting the sustainable use of natural resources, and manufacturing environmentally responsible jute-based products that contribute to reducing plastic pollution. As a producer of eco-friendly packaging and lifestyle products, we recognize our responsibility to minimize environmental impacts across our operations and supply chain. This commitment supports long-term business sustainability, meets customer and stakeholder expectations, enhances operational efficiency, and contributes to a cleaner and more sustainable future for our employees, communities, and the environment.

Environmental considerations are integrated into our business decisions, manufacturing processes, and supply chain activities. We establish annual objectives and targets to improve resource efficiency, reduce waste, manage environmental risks, and strengthen operational performance.

We provide the necessary resources, responsibilities, and employee awareness to achieve these objectives and encourage continuous improvement through practical initiatives, innovation, and collaboration with suppliers and business partners.
declaration.scope:
This policy applies to all employees, contractual workers, contractors, partners, customers, stakeholders, and other persons acting on behalf of Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. across its applicable sites and operations.

It covers environmental aspects throughout the product lifecycle, including raw material sourcing, manufacturing, storage, distribution, use, and end-of-life management.

Energy and Climate: Promote energy-conscious operating practices and improve the efficiency of machinery, lighting, utilities, and other significant energy-consuming activities.
Assess opportunities to adopt renewable energy and lower-carbon technologies as part of future facility and equipment planning.
Maintain a structured approach to identifying significant emission sources and selecting practical measures to reduce their climate impact.
Regularly review energy performance, identify areas of inefficient consumption, and implement appropriate improvement measures.
Build employee awareness of energy conservation and climate-related responsibilities through communication, training, and participation in energy-saving initiatives.
Promote the replacement or upgrading of inefficient lighting systems with energy-efficient alternatives wherever technically and operationally feasible.
Water Stewardship: Improve domestic water-use efficiency through responsible consumption practices, employee awareness, and measures that reduce unnecessary water use.
Strengthen water conservation across operations by optimizing processes, improving housekeeping practices, and reducing avoidable freshwater consumption.
Promote the recovery, reuse, and recycling of suitable wastewater where technically and operationally feasible.
Promote rainwater harvesting and its beneficial use for suitable non-potable applications at applicable facilities.
Maintain water pipelines, tanks, valves, and other high-use systems through preventive inspections, timely maintenance, and prompt correction of identified leaks.
Maintain appropriate wastewater treatment, testing, monitoring, and discharge controls to prevent water pollution and meet applicable requirements.
Regularly assess water-related risks across operations and implement appropriate measures to manage risks associated with water availability, consumption, and potential impacts on water resources.
Air Quality: Integrate practical measures into operations to prevent and minimize air emissions at their source.
Maintain appropriate controls for activities that may generate dust, fumes, particulate matter, or other air emissions.
Promote proper operation and regular maintenance of machinery and emission-control systems.
Encourage cleaner technologies, efficient operating methods, and lower-impact alternatives where technically and commercially feasible.
Periodically review air-emission performance and identify opportunities to strengthen emission-control practices.
Responsible Materials and Waste: Promote practices that reduce the generation of hazardous and non-hazardous waste at source through efficient processes and responsible material use.
Encourage the substitution, reformulation, or reduction of hazardous chemicals with safer alternatives where technically feasible.
Maintain responsible chemical management practices and regularly review applicable regulatory requirements and customer RSL requirements.
Promote segregation, reuse, recycling, and recovery of waste materials wherever technically and operationally feasible.
Ensure hazardous and non-recyclable waste is handled, stored, transported, and disposed of responsibly through authorized or approved channels.
Sustainable Product Design: Consider durability, resource efficiency, recyclability, and environmental attributes when selecting materials for new products.
Encourage practical design changes that reduce material use without compromising product quality, functionality, or durability.
Avoid unnecessary packaging and favor simpler, recyclable, reusable, or lower-impact packaging solutions where appropriate.
Consider the environmental impacts of materials and products from development through use and end-of-life, and use these considerations to guide product improvements.
End-of-Life Responsibility: Encourage customers and business partners to manage used products and packaging through appropriate reuse, recycling, composting, or disposal channels.
Provide practical information to relevant customers on available options for responsible product and packaging disposal.
Explore collaboration with customers, recyclers, and other relevant stakeholders to improve product recovery and end-of-life management.
Promote approaches that help keep suitable products and materials out of landfill and support their return to productive use where feasible.
Foster better cross-functional collaboration between design, manufacturing, and marketing teams and Encourage innovation through improved access to past designs and knowledge sharing.
Conduct an annual review of end-of-life practices for major product categories and document identified improvement opportunities.
Customer Health & Product Safety: Maintain appropriate controls to ensure products are safe and suitable for their intended use.
Integrate quality and safety checks into relevant stages of product development, production, inspection, and dispatch.
Provide relevant product-use, care, handling, and safety information where necessary to support safe use.
Review product quality and safety issues and use customer feedback, complaints, and internal findings to strengthen product controls.
Environmental Compliance: Maintain a structured system for identifying, recording, and monitoring applicable environmental licenses, permits, consents, and renewal dates.
Establish clear responsibilities and advance planning to ensure environmental approvals are renewed before their expiry.
Regularly evaluate applicable environmental obligations and integrate relevant requirements into operational practices.
Review compliance processes periodically and strengthen controls where gaps, delays, or changes in regulatory requirements are identified.
Natural Environment & Green Cover: Maintain or enhance green areas within and around applicable facilities, with progress reviewed annually through 2030.
Monitor newly planted trees and vegetation annually and take reasonable measures to maintain healthy growth and replacement where required.
Maintain existing green areas and landscaping in a manner appropriate to the site and local environmental conditions.
Prefer locally suitable and low-maintenance plant species when developing or improving green areas.
Promote landscaping practices that minimize unnecessary water use, chemical use, and environmental disturbance.
Support practical initiatives that enhance the surrounding environment and contribute to ecological awareness among employees and the local community.

policy.monitoring:
Environmental performance data relating to energy consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, water usage, air emissions, waste management, product stewardship, environmental compliance, and other relevant indicators shall be compiled and reviewed periodically.

The Environmental Management Representative (EMR) or designated Environmental Officer shall prepare environmental performance reports for Senior Management, highlighting progress against objectives and targets, key environmental risks, compliance status, incidents, and improvement opportunities.

Environmental incidents, spills, leaks, non-compliance issues, complaints, and near-miss events shall be reported through established reporting channels, investigated appropriately, and supported by corrective and preventive actions where required.

Findings from environmental monitoring, audits, inspections, and risk assessments shall be communicated to relevant functions to support continual improvement.

Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. may communicate relevant environmental performance information to customers, regulatory authorities, certification bodies, investors, business partners, and other interested stakeholders, as appropriate.

Environmental disclosures, reports, certifications, and regulatory submissions shall be prepared in accordance with applicable legal requirements, customer obligations, and recognized reporting practices where relevant.

Environmental performance information shall be reviewed prior to external communication to ensure accuracy, consistency, and transparency.

Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. shall engage with customers, suppliers, employees, regulatory authorities, local communities, industry associations, and other relevant stakeholders on environmental matters where appropriate.

Stakeholder feedback, concerns, expectations, and improvement suggestions shall be considered during the review of environmental objectives, targets, programs, and management practices.

The Company shall promote open communication and cooperation with relevant stakeholders to support responsible environmental management and continual improvement.
policy.reviewMechanism:
Environmental objectives, targets, and key performance indicators relating to energy consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, water stewardship, air quality, waste management, product stewardship, environmental compliance, and green cover initiatives shall be reviewed annually.

Progress against established targets, environmental performance trends, compliance status, and improvement initiatives shall be evaluated through Management Review Meetings.

Key achievements, challenges, risks, and opportunities for improvement shall be identified and documented to support informed decision-making.

Findings from environmental monitoring, audits, inspections, risk assessments, incident investigations, and stakeholder feedback shall be used to identify opportunities for continual improvement.

Corrective and preventive actions shall be implemented where necessary to address non-conformities, environmental incidents, compliance gaps, or performance concerns.

Environmental objectives, targets, programs, and operational controls shall be updated periodically to improve environmental performance and address emerging environmental issues.

The Environmental Management Representative (EMR) shall review this Policy at least once every two years, or earlier if significant changes occur in legal requirements, business operations, environmental risks, stakeholder expectations, or industry best practices.

Any revisions to the Policy shall be approved by Senior Management and communicated to relevant employees, contractors, and other interested parties as appropriate.

Relevant training, awareness programs, and communication activities shall be conducted to ensure continued understanding and implementation of the updated Policy.
